WHICH ANKLE THE PRODUCT USES IS SETTLED (COMPARISON.html finding 4). Three independent readings agree that ankle_left is the SHIPPED part and that ankle_l_v1 is NOT a later revision of it but the ROLLER variant's ankle. (1) MJCF inventory: ankle_left/ankle_right appear in three of Pollen's five model files, always beside foot_left/foot_right/sole_left/sole_right and never beside the roller kit; ankle_l_v1/ankle_r_v1 appear in two, always beside roller_blade/tire/rim and never beside a foot or a sole. The HF space README calls legs "the default" and rollers "the wheeled skating variant". (2) The vertical screw, measured on four meshes: ankle_left Ø2.2000 at (50.0000, 4.5020) against foot_left's Ø1.6000 pilot at (50.0000, 4.5020) — the same (x, y) to 0.0000 mm; ankle_l_v1 Ø2.2000 at (50.1090, -5.5000) against roller_blade's Ø1.6000 pilot at (50.1090, -5.5000) — again 0.0000 mm. Each ankle is drilled for its own counterpart, which one revision of one part would not be. (3) The bearing pocket: ankle_left Ø15.0000 x 2.3000 behind a Ø14.0000 window, which is the measured OD of the 15x10x3 ring Pollen ships; ankle_l_v1 Ø15.2000 x 2.0000 behind a Ø16.7000 window — 0.2000 mm larger, so they do not even take the same fit. PHOTOGRAPHIC CHECK, read back the same day: images/store/store_microduck-inside-the-box.png labels the box "1 x Microduck, 1 x Battery, 1 x USB-C Cable, 1 x Gamepad" and shows a two-legged duck on FEET with a soft sole — no wheel, rim, tire, roller blade or spare ankle in the box; store_microduck-cream-standing-profile-left.jpg shows the same foot in profile. STILL OPEN and not affecting this answer: whether Pollen sells the roller kit separately. The artifact is this folder's copy of out/laneT/ankle-revision.json, written by tools/ankle_revision.py at the repo root and copied here because a ledger row's artifact path resolves against its own iteration folder.
